title: Destructive action confirmation
description: A confirmation pattern scaled to risk: reversible actions use undo instead of a dialog; irreversible ones use a modal dialog that names the object and the consequence, with the destructive button labeled by the action; the highest-risk actions require typing the object name.
intent: Prevent accidental data loss without adding friction to routine, reversible actions.
characteristics: risk ladder: undo, then confirm dialog, then type-to-confirm
dialog title and button name the action ("Delete project")
consequence stated concretely (what is lost, who is affected)
cancel is the default focus for irreversible actions
danger color plus text, never color alone
interaction: Dialog opens on the trigger, traps focus, Escape cancels, and focus returns to the trigger; type-to-confirm enables the action only on an exact match; success is confirmed and the user lands somewhere sensible.
responsive: Dialog fits narrow screens with buttons stacked, destructive action last; never relies on hover.
accessibility: Native dialog element or role="alertdialog" with aria-labelledby and aria-describedby; initial focus on the least destructive control; button labels are explicit verbs, not "OK".
limitations: Overused confirmations train users to click through; reserve them for irreversible actions.
Undo needs backend support for delayed deletion.
